### BCS-32 — General-state MCMC ergodicity and mixing
**Pages:** mcmc-ergodicity-and-mixing / mcmc-ergodicity-and-mixing-examples. **Scope:** On a countably generated measurable state space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ with probability kernel $P$, define $\phi$-irreducibility for nonzero $\sigma$-finite $\phi$ by: every $A$ with $\phi(A)>0$ is reached with positive probability from every $x$ at some finite time. Define aperiodicity by absence of a cyclic partition of period $d>1$; define Harris recurrence by hitting every $\phi$-positive set almost surely from every starting state. Define $C$ to be $(m,\epsilon,
u)$-small when $P^m(x,A)\ge\epsilon
u(A)$ for all $x\in C,A\in\mathcal X$, with $
u$ a probability measure; define a drift pair by measurable finite $V:\mathsf X	o[1,\infty)$ and $PV\le\lambda V+b1_C$ for $0<\lambda<1,b<\infty$. Distinguish: (i) a $\phi$-irreducible aperiodic chain with invariant probability on a countably generated space converges in $\|P^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{TV}$ for $\pi$-almost every start; Harris recurrence upgrades this to every start; (ii) for a $\phi$-irreducible, aperiodic chain with invariant probability, an $m$-step small-set minorization, and a drift function finite $\pi$-a.e., the small-set/drift hypotheses imply geometric ergodicity with a bound $\|P^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{TV}\le M V(x)r^n$ for constants $M<\infty,r<1$; (iii) uniform ergodicity is convergence at a geometric rate uniformly in $x$ and is tied to whole-space minorization. **Proof route:** Supply the small-set coupling/regeneration argument and the drift-to-geometric bound, including any petite-to-small lemma used, or state and prove an exact alternative theorem. Do not import the countable-state ergodic theorem as a general-state result. **Examples:** reducible and periodic finite chains; a sticky general-state chain; drift/minorization illustration. **Requires:** BCS-29, BCS-30, BCS-31; `def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws`. **Sources:** Roberts–Rosenthal (2004), §§3.2–3.5, 4.1–4.6, pp. 16–41; Jones (2004), §§1–4, PDF pp. 1–14. Their Theorems 4 and 9 cite small-set conversion results, so the new Cat3 proof must provide the specific conversion/coupling step it uses.
